evidence:
tls.lisp:1026-1035 fnn-tls-ssc-write-new: `(fnn-open path (logior ... o-creat o-excl ...)) (unwind-protect (progn (fnn-write-all ...) (fnn-fsync-file fd)) (fnn-close fd))` has no unlink on failure.
tls.lisp:1064-1071:
(t (fnn-tls-ssc-write-new key-path (second key) #o600)
   (handler-bind ((error (lambda (condition) ... (ignore-errors (sb-posix:unlink key-path)))))
     (fnn-tls-ssc-write-new cert-path (second cert) #o644))
The docstring says neither path exists and that the caller's ACL2 outcome refused that.
fix: In fnn-tls-ssc-write-new, unlink PATH when the write or fsync fails after the file was created. Better still, write both files to staged names and rename them into place only after both are durable, then fsync the directory.
reviewer: fnn-tls-ssc-write-new (tls.lisp:1026-1035) does O_CREAT|O_EXCL, then write-all and fsync inside unwind-protect, and only closes the fd on failure; it never unlinks. In fnn-tls-self-signed-write (1064-1071), a failed key write leaves a partial key file. A failed cert write unlinks only key-path and leaves the partial cert-path. A retry then fails the lstat-based ACL2 outcome (operator.lisp:150-153), so the operator has to delete the file by hand. This only happens on ENOSPC or EIO during an operator command.
scenario: ENOSPC or EIO during the key write leaves a truncated key-path. If the cert write fails after O_CREAT, the handler unlinks the key but leaves a truncated cert-path. In both cases a retry is refused by ACL2's 'path exists' outcome (and by O_EXCL), so the operator must find and delete a half-written file by hand. A truncated key or cert also sits where `run` will later try to load it.
title: Self-signed pair writer leaves partial key or cert files behind, and the next run is refused because the paths exist
